questions.question: What is RAG?
relevant_passages: RAG retrieves relevant external information and supplies it to a language model.
questions.reference_answer: RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: it retrieves relevant external information and supplies it to a language model so the answer is grounded in source documents.

questions.question: What does chunk overlap do?
relevant_passages: Overlap repeats the end of one chunk at the start of the next so context is not lost across chunk boundaries.
questions.reference_answer: Overlap preserves context across chunk boundaries by repeating the end of one chunk at the start of the next.

questions.question: Why does brute-force search stop scaling?
relevant_passages: Brute-force search compares the query against every stored vector, so cost grows linearly with the number of documents.
questions.reference_answer: Brute-force search compares the query against every stored vector, so its cost grows linearly with corpus size.

questions.question: What is the capital of Mars?
What is token-aware chunking?
relevant_passages: Token-aware chunking targets a chunk size measured in approximate tokens rather than characters.
questions.reference_answer: Token-aware chunking targets a chunk size measured in approximate tokens rather than characters, using a rule of thumb of four characters per token.

questions.question: How does Markdown-heading-aware chunking work?
relevant_passages: This strategy splits on Markdown headings (#, ##, etc.), keeping each heading with its following content; falls back to fixed-size for oversized sections.
questions.reference_answer: Markdown-heading-aware chunking splits on Markdown headings, keeping each heading with its following content, and falls back to fixed-size chunking for large sections.

questions.question: What is cosine similarity?
relevant_passages: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors.
questions.reference_answer: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors, ranging from -1 (opposite) to 1 (identical direction).

questions.question: When is RAG not a framework?
relevant_passages: RAG is a pipeline, not a framework. You can build it with a few hundred lines of Python.
questions.reference_answer: RAG is a pipeline, not a framework — it can be built with plain Python without orchestration libraries.

questions.question: Can a PDF contain no extractable text?
relevant_passages: V02 handles malformed files including PDFs with no extractable text.
questions.reference_answer: Yes, some PDFs contain no extractable text (e.g., scanned images). V02 reports these as ingestion errors.

questions.question: What are the trade-offs of small vs large chunks?
relevant_passages: Small chunks: precise matches, but each chunk may lack context. Large chunks: more context per chunk, but lower precision and more tokens sent to the model.
questions.reference_answer: Small chunks give precise matches but may lack context; large chunks give more context per chunk but lower precision and use more tokens.
